builds.howItPlays: You take a battlefield early with a cheap unit, and every time you win a fight there you can exhaust Rek'Sai to dig into the top of your deck, play a card straight off it, and set the rest aside. You use that early lead to keep finding new units and press your advantage before your opponent can settle in.
builds.whyYou: You like getting ahead early and then squeezing everything you can out of that lead rather than grinding from an even position. Digging through your deck for exactly the right card the moment you win a fight feels rewarding to you. You're comfortable taking some risk in the opening turns because you know a fast start is how this deck is supposed to work.
builds.ratingNotes: Ability: when you conquer, you may exhaust Rek'Sai to reveal the top 2 cards of your deck, play one, then recycle the rest. Pace 6: riftbound.gg calls it an 'off-tempo aggressive strategy' that wants at least nine 2-cost units to build an early lead, faster than a grinding deck but not an all-in rush. Stance 7: hextechanalytics.com calls it 'strongly proactive,' built around winning a fight to unlock the ability, and riftbound.gg agrees the deck turns controlling once it is ahead. Complexity 6.5: hextechanalytics.com calls it 'high,' citing sequencing of small units and resource allocation across battlefields, while riftbound.gg calls the early game more straightforward; I split the difference. Variance 5.5: hextechanalytics.com warns 'the Legend cannot help before you conquer, losing the early board leaves the deck dependent on the cards already in hand,' so the game can swing hard on that first fight. Confidence: high, both guides describe the same conquer-then-dig loop and the same early-game dependency. Reviewer: none major.
